title: Risk-Based Inspection in Vietnam: Statutory Checks and API 580
description: How RBI fits Vietnam's technical safety inspection and MOIT petroleum safety rules, where the refineries and gas plants are, and how a remote study runs.
h1: Risk-based inspection for Vietnam's refineries, gas plants and fuel terminals
intro: Vietnam's refineries, gas plants and fuel terminals answer to two sets of rules at once: periodic technical safety inspection of listed equipment by certified inspection organisations, and the safety documents the Ministry of Industry and Trade requires for petroleum activities. Neither tells an owner where inspection effort does the most good between those fixed points. This page is for integrity and inspection engineers at Vietnamese facilities. It covers the framework after the 2025 government reorganisation, the two refineries and the southern gas and petrochemical cluster, what owners usually ask of an outside study, and how Atlantis runs one remotely on Indochina Time.

highlights.p: Statutory inspection dates on listed equipment stay where the certified inspection organisation puts them. A risk-based plan decides what the owner's own inspections cover between and around those dates: which items, which methods, how much coverage and in which turnaround.

Vietnam keeps UTC+7 all year, an hour and a half ahead of India. Workshops sit comfortably inside both working days, the study needs no travel, and anything that must be seen on the plant goes to the owner's inspectors on a written list.

Inspection certificates and maintenance history are usually kept in Vietnamese, vendor data and licensor packages in English. The study works through the owner's bilingual engineers and keeps every equipment tag exactly as the site register writes it.

sections.h: Who regulates pressure equipment after the 2025 reorganisation
p: Vietnam's Law on Occupational Safety and Health of 2015 places the duty on employers to keep machinery and equipment with strict occupational safety requirements in a safe condition. The lists of such equipment take in boilers, pressure vessels, steam and hot-water piping, LPG tanks and fixed metal gas pipelines, among other plant. Listed equipment must pass technical safety inspection by an inspection organisation certified for that class of equipment, before it is put into use and periodically afterwards. The procedures are national documents; for pressure vessels the procedure is QTKĐ 07-2016/BLĐTBXH, issued under Circular 54/2016/TT-BLĐTBXH.

The ministry that wrote those procedures no longer exists in its old form. On 1 March 2025 the Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs was dissolved in a consolidation of government ministries, and its labour functions passed to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The procedures kept their old reference codes. In October 2025 the Ministry of Home Affairs issued Circular 19/2025/TT-BNV, in force from 1 December 2025, which sets out the economic and technical characteristics of occupational safety inspection services and points back to the existing procedures, the pressure vessel one included, rather than replacing them. If one of those procedures is later amended or replaced, the circular applies the new text.

Ministries with a sector of their own also certify inspection organisations for the equipment they manage. The Ministry of Industry and Trade, through its industrial safety and environment agency, publishes a list of organisations certified to inspect equipment such as power plant boilers, industrial boilers and pressure vessels, steam and hot-water piping, LPG tanks and fixed gas pipelines. For an owner the working question is plain: which body inspects each item, under which procedure, and when its next periodic inspection falls due.

sections.h: Periodic technical safety inspection and the space RBI works in
p: Each inspection procedure provides for a first inspection, periodic inspections and unscheduled inspections when circumstances require them, and the inspection organisation records the result together with the next due date. An owner's RBI study does not move those dates. Where a statutory inspection is due, the study treats the date as fixed and plans the owner's own work around it.

That still leaves a great deal for risk to decide. A statutory inspection establishes that an item may continue in service under the procedure; it does not tell the owner which damage mechanism threatens which nozzle, whether last turnaround's thickness readings could have found the localised corrosion the process now produces, or which of several hundred piping circuits deserve corrosion mapping at the next shutdown. How much of a site falls within the statutory lists depends on equipment class and the list criteria, so the study confirms item by item which equipment carries a statutory date and which is planned only under the owner's procedures.

sections.h: Petroleum safety documents under the Ministry of Industry and Trade
p: Refineries, gas processing plants, LNG terminals, depots and pipelines are oil and gas works, and their safety is governed through the Ministry of Industry and Trade. Decree 13/2011/NĐ-CP on the safety of onshore oil and gas works, amended by Decree 25/2019/NĐ-CP, sets the framework for those works. Circular 40/2018/TT-BCT, amended in 2025 by Circular 38/2025/TT-BCT, sets out three safety documents for petroleum activities on land and at sea: a safety management programme, a risk assessment report and an emergency response plan, each prepared before construction and operation and revised before major changes. Since the 2025 amendment the ministry's industrial safety agency approves the documents for works at the scale the ministry appraises, while provincial People's Committees approve them for the remaining works in their province, smaller petroleum depots and LPG installations among them. The ministry has also consulted on further changes to the circular, so owners should confirm which version their documents were prepared under.

The risk assessment report is a process safety document. It examines release scenarios, their consequences and the risk they carry to people and property, and the circular, as amended in 2025, still requires it to be brought up to date every five years as well as before modifications, changes of capacity or technology, and decommissioning. An RBI study shares some of its vocabulary, probability and consequence, but answers a narrower question: how inspection should be planned so that deterioration is found before it leads to a loss of containment. The two documents ought to agree on fluids, inventories and consequence areas, and the RBI register can give the risk assessment better information about equipment condition, but neither replaces the other.

This has a practical edge. When the risk assessment report is next revised, or a modification triggers a revision, the same isolatable sections and inventories should appear in both documents. A study that begins by reading the current report avoids two registers telling a regulator different stories about the same equipment.

sections.h: Petrovietnam, joint ventures and the standards they bring
p: Most of Vietnam's refining and gas assets sit within the Vietnam Oil and Gas Group, Petrovietnam or PVN. BSR, in which PVN holds about 92 percent, runs the Dung Quat refinery; PV GAS runs gas processing, pipelines and the Thi Vai LNG import terminal; and PVFCCo operates the Phu My fertilizer plant. Two of the largest plants have foreign shareholders. Nghi Son Refinery and Petrochemical is owned 35.1 percent each by Idemitsu Kosan and Kuwait Petroleum, 25.1 percent by PVN and 4.7 percent by Mitsui Chemicals, while Long Son Petrochemicals is wholly owned by SCG Chemicals of Thailand.

Each of these brings its own engineering practice. A Petrovietnam company may work to group procedures, a joint venture may carry over practice from its Japanese or Kuwaiti shareholders, and a Thai-owned complex may follow its parent's standards. None of that is assumed. The first task of an outside study is to establish which document governs inspection planning for each asset, which risk matrix the owner has adopted and who can approve a departure, and to write those answers into the study basis before any data is requested.

Where a shareholder runs a group-level RBI programme and the site keeps its own register, the study maps one onto the other so that a given vessel carries the same damage mechanisms, risk category and next inspection in both. That prevents the familiar drift in which a group report and a site plan disagree about a date and nobody can say which is right.

sections.h: Where Vietnam's refining, gas and petrochemical capacity sits
p: Vietnam has two crude oil refineries, one on the central coast and one in the north-central province of Thanh Hoa, and a gas and petrochemical cluster on the south-east coast around Vung Tau. Together the two refineries meet about 70 percent of domestic fuel demand, and the balance is imported. In normal conditions the country exports part of its own crude production and imports crude feedstock for the refineries, so crude tanks, jetties and product import terminals matter to national supply far more than the small number of plants suggests.

Fuel import depots and distribution terminals serve the coast and the main river systems beyond those clusters. Where a depot's inspection records are thin, a qualitative screen is usually the right first step, because it shows which tanks and lines need data collected before any meaningful risk can be calculated.

sections.h: A long coastline and three climates
p: Vietnam spans nearly fifteen degrees of latitude, and its three industrial areas sit in different weather. The north-central coast around Nghi Son has hot, humid summers, a spell of hot, dry westerly wind in early summer and a cool, damp winter under the north-east monsoon. The central coast at Dung Quat takes its heaviest rain and most of its tropical storms in autumn and early winter. The south-east around Vung Tau is tropical, with a wet season from about May to November and a dry season for the rest of the year, and lies south of the usual typhoon tracks.

What the three share is moisture and salt. Every major site is on the sea or an estuary, and corrosion under insulation on carbon and low-alloy steel, chloride cracking of insulated austenitic stainless steel and atmospheric corrosion of jetty lines, pipe racks and tank roofs are the external mechanisms that most often lift items in a Vietnamese register. Storms and floods belong in the reassessment triggers too: wind-damaged cladding lets water into insulation, and flood water around tank foundations and buried lines changes soil-side conditions in ways the next inspection plan should reflect.

sections.h: What Vietnamese owners usually ask an outside RBI study for
p: Requests from Vietnamese facilities tend to fall into a handful of patterns.
list: A first RBI programme for a refinery or gas plant unit, with damage mechanisms, risk ranking and inspection plans aligned to the dates that statutory inspection already fixes.
Scoping a major turnaround: which vessels to open, which can be assessed on stream and which piping circuits need corrosion mapping rather than spot readings.
Reassessing damage mechanisms and integrity operating windows when the crude slate changes, before new grades start to run.
A baseline register for new units, built from design data, manufacturer's data reports and first readings, so that the first in-service inspection is planned on evidence.
Restart planning for equipment that has been preserved or idle, with a list of what must be inspected before it returns to service.
Tank-by-tank RBI for a crude or product terminal, covering floor and annular plate condition, cathodic protection records and floating-roof drainage.
Mapping a shareholder's group RBI register onto the site's own register and its statutory inspection records.

sections.h: Running the study on Indochina Time
p: Vietnam keeps Indochina Time, UTC+7, throughout the year. Atlantis works from Hyderabad, ninety minutes behind, and from Houston, twelve hours behind in the US summer and thirteen in the US winter. Video workshops are booked in the Vietnamese morning and early afternoon, which falls within the Indian working morning, and analysis and drafting continue from Houston while the plant sleeps. The Lunar New Year holiday takes many engineers away from site, so workshop calendars are set around it rather than through it.

Documents arrive through a data room that the owner controls. Inspection certificates, maintenance records and operating procedures in Vietnamese are reviewed with the owner's bilingual engineers, or translated through the owner's own arrangements, and deliverables are written in English with Vietnamese tags and document numbers left exactly as they are. Where the owner's rules restrict what may leave its systems, reviews run by screen share and the study records which version of each document it relied on.

The study is designed so that nobody needs to travel. Insulation condition, injection points, dead legs, small-bore connections and tank annular plates go on a verification list for the owner's inspectors or inspection contractor, and their findings are fed back into the assessment before the plan is issued.

sections.h: Decisions that stay with the owner and with Vietnamese bodies
p: Statutory technical safety inspection and its conclusions belong to the certified inspection organisation; petroleum safety documents are approved by the Ministry of Industry and Trade or the provincial department; and inspection intervals outside those regimes are decided by the owner's inspection authority. Atlantis is not a licensed Vietnamese inspection organisation and does not act as inspector of record. The study recommends and documents, and the owner decides.

If inspection finds damage that the construction code does not accept, the engineering assessment that follows stays with the owner's engineer, and the register is updated with its result before the next plan is issued. Atlantis does not carry out fitness-for-service assessments.

faqs.q: Can an RBI study extend the periodic inspection date recorded for a pressure vessel?
faqs.a: No. Periodic technical safety inspection of listed equipment is carried out by a certified inspection organisation under the national procedure, and its due date stands whatever an owner's study concludes. What the study changes is the owner's own inspection: which items are opened at a turnaround, which methods and how much coverage are used, and which items are watched more closely between statutory inspections. Statutory dates go into the register as fixed constraints, and the plan is built around them.

faqs.q: Is the risk assessment report required by the Ministry of Industry and Trade the same as an RBI study?
faqs.a: No. The risk assessment report under Circular 40/2018/TT-BCT is a process safety document about release scenarios and their consequences, prepared by the operator, updated every five years and revised before major changes. An RBI study plans inspection so that deterioration is found before it causes a release. The two should use the same fluids, inventories and isolatable sections, and the study is built to be consistent with the current report, but it is never presented as that report.

faqs.q: Which ministry deals with occupational safety inspection now that the labour ministry has gone?
faqs.a: The Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs was dissolved on 1 March 2025 and its labour functions passed to the Ministry of Home Affairs, which in October 2025 issued a circular on occupational safety inspection services that refers back to the existing inspection procedures. Sector ministries, the Ministry of Industry and Trade among them, certify inspection organisations for the equipment they manage. Owners should confirm the issuing body behind each certificate in their register.

faqs.q: Can Atlantis carry out the statutory technical safety inspection at our site?
faqs.a: No. Statutory inspection in Vietnam is done by inspection organisations certified for the equipment concerned, and Atlantis is not one of them. Its role is the engineering study around that system: damage mechanisms, risk ranking, inspection plans for the owner's own programme and the data work behind them. The study is delivered remotely, and the owner's inspectors or inspection contractor carry out any field checks it calls for.

faqs.q: Our inspection history is in Vietnamese and partly on paper. Can the study use it?
faqs.a: Yes. Scanned certificates, thickness sheets and maintenance records are reviewed with the owner's bilingual engineers, who help confirm what each record actually shows. Readings are entered against the owner's own tags, and each record is graded for what it can demonstrate. A thickness survey with known locations earns credit against general corrosion; a certificate stating only that a vessel passed does not, by itself, show the condition of a particular nozzle or weld.

In the Vietnamese morning and early afternoon. Vietnam is ninety minutes ahead of Hyderabad, so sessions fall in the Indian morning, and the Houston team carries the analysis on overnight Vietnamese time. Sessions are usually kept to two or three hours so that operations and process engineers can take part without leaving the plant short, and the calendar is planned around the Lunar New Year and the site's turnaround window.

faqs.q: Does anyone from Atlantis need to travel to Vietnam for the study?
faqs.a: The study is built to need no travel. Data comes through the owner's data room, workshops run by video, and anything that has to be seen on the plant, such as damaged insulation, the location of an injection point or the condition of a tank's annular plate, goes on a written verification list for the owner's inspectors or inspection contractor. Their findings are entered into the model before the plan is finalised.

faqs.q: Who approves the inspection intervals that an RBI plan proposes?
faqs.a: The owner. Statutory dates belong to the certified inspection organisation. Intervals in the owner's own programme are approved by its inspection authority under its procedures and, where API 510, API 570 or API 653 have been adopted, by the inspector the owner designates under those codes. Atlantis prepares and documents the recommendations and does not act as inspector of record.
